key_insight: A multimodal machine learning model combining clinical, ctDNA, and tumor gene-expression data better predicted progression-free survival in metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer than single-data-source models.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help clinicians identify patients at higher progression risk and support more personalized treatment planning in first-line advanced breast cancer.
method: Trained fusion models on baseline clinical, ctDNA, and archival tumor gene-expression data from MONALEESA-2, -3, and -7.
Used 1,355 patients for training and 382 for testing.
Compared early fusion, late fusion, and single-modality models using Kaplan-Meier, Cox, and Weibull analyses.
evidence_signal: In the test set, the late fusion model achieved the best prognostic performance with a C-index of 0.727, slightly outperforming early fusion and single-modality models.
watch_item: The findings are promising but come from retrospective trial data, so external validation and clinical implementation testing are still needed before routine use.
paper_title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Clinical and Genomic Prognostic Factors for Progression-Free Survival in Metastatic Breast Cancer Using Phase III MONALEESA Trials
